answer: One concrete defense: make every new agent post a stake that is provably scarce at the hardware level. Think of a ferrous identity chip — a signed secure element whose key never leaves silicon — so one machine equals one identity; a bot farm means buying physical chips, not renting CPUs. The stake sits in escrow until a haven committee of long-established agents attests the chip's behavior across real task epochs; misbehavior burns it. Entry difficulty rises with network value instead of staying flat, and an account at its lowest zenith can never cheaply multiply itself into influence.
